entities.summary: Early presidential elections were held in Sri Lanka on 8 January 2015, nearly two years ahead of schedule. Incumbent President Mahinda Rajapaksa was the ruling United People's Freedom Alliance's candidate, seeking a third term in office after presidential term limits were abolished in 2010 by the 18th amendment to the constitution. The United National Party-led opposition coalition chose to field Maithripala Sirisena, former Minister of Health in Rajapaksa's government and general secretary of the Sri Lanka Freedom Party – the main constituent party of the UPFA – as its common opposition candidate.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: The election led to a constitutional crisis and ultimately resulted in Sirisena's resignation after just over a year in office, prompting new elections in 2019. This event marked a significant shift in Sri Lanka's politics and had regional implications for the country's relations with its neighbors.
